 J U D G M E N T

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of .50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Sri.Akram Pasha S/o Late Basha, in road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 28.01.2023 at about 03.45 p.m., the deceased Sri.Akram Pasha was travelling as an inmate in an Autorickshaw bearing Regn.No.KA-06-AB-1077 from Dobbespet towards Gollahalli and when they reached near Kuthaghatta Cross, at Sharadha Cross- Shivagange Road, Sompura Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru District, the driver of said Autorickshaw drove in a rash and negligent manner at high speed and lost control over the auto due to which the auto capsized.
Due to said accident, deceased sustained fatal injuries.

Thereafter,
deceased was shifted to PHC Dobbespet, wherein first aid treatment was given and he succumbed to the injuries on the way to District Hospital, Tumakur and later body was shifted to PHC Dobbespet and conducted postmortem and handed over the body to petitioners and shifted the body to their native and perform the funeral and obsequies ceremonies for which they have spent a sum of .1,00,000/-.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and was doing labour work and earning a sum of .20,000/- per month.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners lost bread earning member of the family and put to lot of mental agony.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of autorickshaw by its driver.
The respondent No.1 & 2, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
3. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1 not appeared before the tribunal and hence, he has been placed ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed his written statement.

In the Written Statement, the respondent No.2 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.2 also denied age, occupation and income of deceased as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.2 contended that the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further respondent No.2 admitted the aspect of issue of policy pertaining to autorickshaw and contended that the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further the driver of autorickshaw was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
Further contended that the autorickshaw was not having valid permit to ply in place of accident at the time of accident.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.

Hence,
prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioners prove that the husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioner No.2 & 3, son of petitioner No.4 and brother of petitioner No.5 namely Akram Pasha succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 28.01.2023 at around 03.45 p.m., near Kuthaghatta Cross, Sharadha Cross, Shivagange Road,
Sompura Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru District, while he was travelling as an inmate in Autorickshaw bearing Regn.No.KA-06-AB- 1077, due to the rash and negligent driving of said vehicle by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to substantiate the contention of the petition, the Petitioner No.1/wife of deceased got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9 and closed her side of evidence.

On the other hand, the Superintendent by name Sri.H.G.Devaraju of RTO got examined as RW.1 and respondent insurance company examined its Manager as RW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 to 6 and closed their side of evidence.

7. Heard arguments on both sides and perused the materials available on records.
8.
This Tribunal answers the above issues as below:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: 10. The Petitioner No.1/wife of deceased Sri.Akram Pasha examined as PW.1.

In the chief- examination, PW.1 deposed that her husband was travelling in autorickshaw bearing Regn.No.KA-06- AB-1077 as an inmate and due to the rash and negligent driving of the said auto by its driver, the accident occurred.

In order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of autorickshaw, the petitioners produced Ex.P.2 First Information lodged by brother of deceased by name Sri.Asim Pasha with police on 29.01.2023 pertaining to accident occurred on 28.01.2023.
On the basis of first information lodged by brother of deceased, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 304(A) of IPC and U/s.187 of M.V.Act.
In first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of autorickshaw by its driver.
The petitioners furnished the mahazar as well as sketch which are marked as Ex.P.3 and P.4.
The said documents disclose the aspect of police visiting the spot of accident after registration of FIR.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to haven caused due to negligence on the part of driver of autorickshaw.
The said documents also disclose negligence on the part of driver of autorickshaw in the cause of accident.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that the facts at place of accident, as described in mahazar and sketch, are contrary to actual facts.
Ex.P.5 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to the vehicle are mentioned.
The said document discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The driver or owner of the offending vehicle not provided satisfactory explanation regarding the manner in which damages are caused to the vehicles.
The driver or owner of rickshaw not provided proper explanation regarding the manner in which damages were caused to the vehicle, if the vehicle was not involved in the accident.
The said document clearly indicates involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
Ex . P.6
- Inquest Report.

Ex.P7 is the PM report,
wherein deceased Sri.Akram Pasha is stated to have died due to hypovolemic shock secondary to injury to internal organs.
The I.O., after detailed investigation filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 338 & 304(A) of IPC as per Ex.P.8.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending autorickshaw.
In the final report, there is mention about negligence on the part of driver of the autorickshaw.
The documents furnished by petitioners disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of autorickshaw in the cause of accident.
The respondents not placed any materials in order to rebut or disprove the documents furnished by the petitioners related to the aspect of negligence.
The owner or driver of the car does not appear to have challenged the FIR as well as final report filed by the police against the driver of offending vehicle.
The correctness of investigation does not appear to have been challenged by respondents in any manner.
In the cross examination of PW.1 also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited from the witness.

sentences.text: The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the documents furnished by the petitioners are to be looked into in order to ascertain the aspect of negligence.
The materials placed before the Tribunal points towards the negligence on the part of driver of offending car in the cause of accident.
So, the oral and documentary evidence placed by the petitioners discloses that the accident was caused due to rash and negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of petitioners coupled with the documents produced before this tribunal, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Autorickshaw bearing Regn.No.KA-06-AB-1077 by its driver and deceased succumbed to injuries.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like age, avocation, income of deceased, conveyance charges, funeral and obsequies, towards of loss of love and affection, etc.

(A) Towards dependency and loss of future earnings:
(i) In the petition the age of the deceased Sri.Akram Pasha is shown as 38 years.
In order to prove age of deceased, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.9 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 1983.
As per the document furnished by petitioners, the age of the deceased appears to be 40 years at the time of accident.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to dispute or rebut the document furnished by petitioners related to the age of deceased.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the document furnished by petitioners is to be considered for ascertaining the age of deceased.
The accident occurred on 28.01.2023.
As per the materials furnished before the Tribunal, the age of deceased was 40 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme court of India in Smt.Sarla Verma case '15' multiplier is applicable in the present case.
(ii) The petitioners contended that deceased Sri.Akram Pasha was doing labour work and earning a sum of .20,000/- per month.
In order to prove the occupation and income of deceased, the petitioner not produced any documents.
The petitioners not furnished satisfactory materials in order to substantiate their contention related to occupation and income of deceased.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials related to occupation and income of deceased, notional income is to be considered.
By considering the facts and circumstances of case, the notional income of deceased is considered as .16,000/- per month.

In Hem Raj V/s the Oriental Insurance Company Ltd and others the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that there cannot be distinction where there is positive evidence of income and where minimum income is determined on guess work in the facts and circumstances of a case.

Hence, in view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioners are entitled for additional 25% to the established income.

The established income of the deceased is .16,000/- and 25% of .16,000/-
is .4,000/-.
So, the total gross income of deceased was .16,000/- + .4,000/- = .20,000/- per month.

As per the materials on record, the deceased Sri.Akram Pasha is married, having wife,
children, mother and sister of deceased.
In order to prove the same, the petitioners have produced notarized copies of Aadhaar cards, which are marked as Ex.P9.
On perusal of the same it reveals that petitioners No.1 to 5 are wife, children, mother and sister of deceased respectively.
The said document discloses the relationship of petitioners with that of the deceased.
The materials on record disclose that petitioners are dependents on the income of deceased.
Hence, petitioner No.1 to 5 are considered as dependents of deceased.

As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Smt.Sarla Verma case where number of dependent family members is 4 to 6, 1/4th has to be deducted from the gross income of deceased towards his personal expenses and remaining is to be taken as income towards dependency.

sentences.text: 15. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondent No.1 & 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Autorickshaw bearing Regn.No.KA-06-AB- 1077 by its driver.
The materials on record reveals that the respondent No.1 is the owner of offending Autorickshaw, the autorickshaw is having valid policy of insurance at the time of accident.

The respondent No.2 specifically contended that the offending vehicle is not having valid permit to ply over the area of accident and violated the terms of policy conditions and hence, they are not liable to pay compensation.
In order to substantiate the said contention, the respondent No.2 summoned the RTO, Tumkur, who got examined as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 to R.4.
RW.1 stated that the offending vehicle was having permit to ply the vehicle within the radius of 10 kms of Municipal limits of Tumkur.
RW.1 also stated that the permit does not include Dabaspet of Nelamangala Taluk and the said area will not come within the jurisdiction of Tumkur RTO.
RW.1 is cross examined on behalf of petitioner and during the course of cross examination, it is suggested to the witness that the offending vehicle got permit from Nelamangala RTO.
But, no materials are placed before the tribunal to show the aspect of permit being obtained at Nelamangala RTO.
16. RW.1 furnished permit Extract and B- Register Extract of offending vehicle, which are marked as Ex.R.2 & 4.

On perusal of Ex.R.2, it could be noticed that permit with respect to the offending vehicle is given by Regional Transport Authority, Tumkur and permission pertains to movement of vehicle within the radius of 10 Kms in the limits of Tumkur.

As per Ex.R2, the offending vehicle is having permit valid from 25.03.2018 to 24.03.2023, but the permit is limited to ply the vehicle within the radius of 10 kms in town of Municipal limits of Tumkur.

As per the materials on record,
the accident took place at Dabaspet which falls within the jurisdiction of Nelamangala.
The offending vehicle does not appear to have permit to ply the vehicle within the limits of Nelamangala.
Ex.R2 does not disclose the aspect of grant of permit to respondent No.1 to ply the vehicle within the limits of Nelamangala.
Ex. R2
reveals the aspect of offending vehicle not having permit to ply the vehicle within the limits of Nelamangala where the accident took place.
The petitioner not produced any materials contrary to Ex.R2.

The petitioner also not furnished the materials to show that the Salma Bi vs Suresh on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121313247/
7 offending vehicle was having valid permit to ply the vehicle within the limits of Nelamangala.

sentences.text: Further, Ex.R4 - B-Register Extract pertaining to the offending vehicle, reflects the aspect of grant of permit to ply the vehicle within the radius of 15 kms in the limits of Tumkur, but the offending vehicle travelled beyond the limits of permit.
The materials on record do not disclose the aspect of possessing permit to ply the vehicle within the limits of Nelamangala.
Ex.R2 & 4 clearly discloses the aspect of granting of permit to ply the vehicle only within the limits of Tumkur Municipal limits Corporation upto the radius of 15 Kms.
It is not forthcoming for the materials on record related to permit being granted for plying the vehicle in the jurisdiction of Nelamangala.
Ex.R2 & 4 substantiates the contention of respondent No.2 regarding plying of vehicle outside the area to which permit was granted.
There is violation of conditions mentioned in the permit by the driver of offending vehicle.
As there is violation of conditions related to permit, the said violation falls under Sec.150 of M.V.Act.
As per Sec.150 of M.V.Act, the insurance company can plead the defence related to violation of permit among other grounds provided under the said provision.
The materials on record clearly disclose the aspect of violation of conditions of permit as well as conditions of policy of insurance by respondent No.1.
It is pertinent to note that respondent No.1 not appeared before the tribunal in order to negate the contention of respondent No.2.

Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 neither appeared nor placed materials to show that the offending vehicle was having valid and effective permit to ply in the area of accident as on the date of accident.

The materials placed on record disclose the aspect of violation of conditions of permit by respondent No.1.
17.
The accident in question occurred on 28.01.2023 i.e., subsequent to the amendment which came into effect from 1/4/2022.
As per the provisions of Sec.150 of Motor Vehicles, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability to pay compensation if there is violation of terms of the policy.

In the present case, the driver of Autorickshaw bearing Regn.No.KA-06-AB-1077 does not appear to have valid permit to drive the vehicle which aspect is forthcoming from the materials placed on record.
The materials on record disclose the aspect of violation of terms of the policy.

Though the policy pertaining to offending vehicle is in existence at the time of accident, as there is violation of conditions of permit, the insurance company cannot be held liable to pay the compensation.

Further, in view of the amendment to the Act, as discussed supra, no liability can be fastened on the Respondent No.2, to pay the compensation and to recover the same from the Respondent No.1 under pay and recovery theory.

18. The counsel for respondent No.2 relied on the decisions mentioned below in support of their contention:
1. ILR 2012 KAR 6065 of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in between Sri.B.T.Venkatesh Vs. Sri.Jagadeesh Kumar and others.

sentences.text: 19. This Tribunal carefully considered the said decisions and said decisions are applicable to the case on hand.

Accordingly, the Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the liability of paying the Salma Bi vs Suresh on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121313247/
8 compensation to the petitioners is to be fastened solely on the Respondent No.1, who is the owner of the offending vehicle, as he has violated the policy condition by plying the vehicle in the limits to which permit was not valid and effective.
The offending vehicle does not have permit to ply in the limits in which accident occurred.
Respondent No.1 not appeared before the Tribunal in order to controvert the contention of petitioner as well as respondent No.2.
Respondent No.1 neither appeared nor placed materials to show that the vehicle involved in the accident was taken without his permission or knowledge.
Respondent No.1 not appeared before the court and also not put forth any contention contrary to the version of petitioner and respondent No.2.
There is violation of terms of the policy issued by respondent No.2.
As there is violation of terms of the policy, the liability cannot be fastened on respondent No.2 to pay the compensation.
Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.2 is answered Partly in the Affirmative.
20. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of .29,29,900/- (Rupees Twenty Nine Lakhs Twenty Nine Thousand Nine Hundred only) with interest at 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 is solely liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners with interest within two months from the date of award.
This petition against the Respondent No.2 is dismissed.

Out of the total compensation amount, the petitioner No.1 being the wife of deceased is entitled for 40%, petitioner No.2 & 3 are children of deceased are entitled for 20%
each, petitioner No.4 being the mother of deceased is entitled for 10% and petitioner No.5 being the sister of deceased is entitled for 10% of the compensation amount.
In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioner No.1, 60% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1, and 40% of the amount shall be kept in FD for a period of three years.

20% each of compensation amount allotted to the share of minor petitioner No.2 & 3 shall be kept in FD in their names of minor petitioners in any of the Nationalized Bank or Scheduled Bank of the choice of minor guardian for a period of 3 years or till they attains the age of majority whichever is later.
The guardian of petitioner No.1 is entitled for interest that accrues on FD periodically.
In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioner No.4 & 5, entire amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.4 & 5 as amount is meager one.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.
Whether petitioners prove that the husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioner No.2 & 3, son of petitioner No.4 and brother of petitioner No.5 namely Akram Pasha succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 28.01.2023 at around 03.45 p.m., near Kuthaghatta Cross, Sharadha Cross, Shivagange Road,
Sompura Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru District, while he was travelling as an inmate in Autorickshaw bearing Regn.No.KA-06-AB- 1077, due to the rash and negligent driving of said vehicle by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The documents furnished by petitioners disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of autorickshaw in the cause of accident.
The respondents not placed any materials in order to rebut or disprove the documents furnished by the petitioners related to the aspect of negligence.
The owner or driver of the car does not appear to have challenged the FIR as well as final report filed by the police against the driver of offending vehicle.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the documents furnished by the petitioners are to be looked into in order to ascertain the aspect of negligence.
As per the document furnished by petitioners, the age of the deceased appears to be 40 years at the time of accident.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to dispute or rebut the document furnished by petitioners related to the age of deceased.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the document furnished by petitioners is to be considered for ascertaining the age of deceased.
The accident occurred on 28.01.2023.
As per the materials furnished before the Tribunal, the age of deceased was 40 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials related to occupation and income of deceased, notional income is to be considered.
There is violation of conditions mentioned in the permit by the driver of offending vehicle.
As there is violation of conditions related to permit, the said violation falls under Sec.150 of M.V.Act.
As per Sec.150 of M.V.Act, the insurance company can plead the defence related to violation of permit among other grounds provided under the said provision.
The materials on record clearly disclose the aspect of violation of conditions of permit as well as conditions of policy of insurance by respondent No.1.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 neither appeared nor placed materials to show that the offending vehicle was having valid and effective permit to ply in the area of accident as on the date of accident.
The materials placed on record disclose the aspect of violation of conditions of permit by respondent No.1.
17.
The accident in question occurred on 28.01.2023 i.e., subsequent to the amendment which came into effect from 1/4/2022.
As per the provisions of Sec.150 of Motor Vehicles, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability to pay compensation if there is violation of terms of the policy.
In the present case, the driver of Autorickshaw bearing Regn.No.KA-06-AB-1077 does not appear to have valid permit to drive the vehicle which aspect is forthcoming from the materials placed on record.
The materials on record disclose the aspect of violation of terms of the policy.
Though the policy pertaining to offending vehicle is in existence at the time of accident, as there is violation of conditions of permit, the insurance company cannot be held liable to pay the compensation.
Further, in view of the amendment to the Act, as discussed supra, no liability can be fastened on the Respondent No.2, to pay the compensation and to recover the same from the Respondent No.1 under pay and recovery theory.

20. Issue No.3:
In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of .29,29,900/- (Rupees Twenty Nine Lakhs Twenty Nine Thousand Nine Hundred only) with interest at 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 is solely liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners with interest within two months from the date of award.
This petition against the Respondent No.2 is dismissed.
Out of the total compensation amount, the petitioner No.1 being the wife of deceased is entitled for 40%, petitioner No.2 & 3 are children of deceased are entitled for 20%
each, petitioner No.4 being the mother of deceased is entitled for 10% and petitioner No.5 being the sister of deceased is entitled for 10% of the compensation amount.
In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioner No.1, 60% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1, and 40% of the amount shall be kept in FD for a period of three years.
20% each of compensation amount allotted to the share of minor petitioner No.2 & 3 shall be kept in FD in their names of minor petitioners in any of the Nationalized Bank or Scheduled Bank of the choice of minor guardian for a period of 3 years or till they attains the age of majority whichever is later.
The guardian of petitioner No.1 is entitled for interest that accrues on FD periodically.
In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioner No.4 & 5, entire amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.4 & 5 as amount is meager one.
